results.name: Nicaragua
results.key_finding: Why it matters: Nicaragua sits near the bottom of the scale and its newest conduct confirms that. The UN human rights chief said on 22 July 2026 that 46 people are held in arbitrary political detention, lawyers have had credentials revoked without explanation, and 80-year-old Bishop Abelardo Mata has been detained since 29 June with his whereabouts withheld.

results.name: Nike
results.key_finding: Why it matters: a federal jury decided this, so it is a finding and not an allegation. On 22 July 2026 a Portland jury found Nike underpaid and under-promoted engineer Heather Hender because of her gender, awarding about 19,730 dollars in damages plus at least 7.5 million dollars in punitive damages after an eight-year case.

results.name: Microsoft AI
results.key_finding: Why it matters: the layoff figure that flagged Microsoft was a year old. The roughly 9,000 cuts at about 4 per cent of workforce happened in July 2025; the real July 2026 figure is about 4,800 roles at 2.1 per cent, alongside WARN Act compliance investigations and union legal action over the Xbox cuts.

results.name: UPS
results.key_finding: Why it matters: the case that flagged UPS had already closed. A former driver 238 million dollar discrimination award was cut to nothing on appeal and the parties settled confidentially in May 2026, leaving no published admission, no disclosed amount and no systemic remedy.

results.name: Isomorphic Labs
results.key_finding: Why it matters: this is one of the few entities flagged this cycle for doing something good. On 16 July 2026 Google DeepMind and Isomorphic Labs published a joint bioresilience approach, and Isomorphic set up a dedicated unit to design medical countermeasures quickly when an outbreak begins.

results.name: Honduras
results.key_finding: Why it matters: Honduras evicted a community from land a regional court had already ruled was theirs. More than 200 police entered the Garifuna community of San Juan on 6 July 2026 with tear gas and live ammunition, and a judge then reclassified the ancestral-land case as organised crime.

results.name: Papua New Guinea
results.key_finding: Why it matters: Papua New Guinea prosecuted protest rather than answering it. Police arrested six men for burning the national flag at a demonstration against the Bush Wara eviction in Port Moresby, a settlement that had housed about 5,000 people.

results.name: Islamabad
results.key_finding: Why it matters: the deaths that flagged Islamabad were not caused by Islamabad. At least 31 people have been killed since late June 2026 in Pakistan-administered Kashmir by federal and regional authorities, several hundred kilometres from the city, so the attribution rule applies and the score is unchanged.

results.name: Jordan
results.key_finding: Why it matters: the event that flagged Jordan was harm done to Jordan, not by it. The Iranian Revolutionary Guard struck the Al-Azraq air base on Jordanian territory on 20 July 2026, which under the attribution rule does not lower the Jordanian score.

results.name: Clearview AI
results.key_finding: Why it matters: the one repair Clearview AI had on the table has been taken off it. On 13 July 2026 the Seventh Circuit vacated approval of its biometric-privacy class settlement over unequal shares by state, so no repair is in place for the people whose faces were scraped.

results.name: Ukraine
results.key_finding: Why it matters: the July 2026 deaths were inflicted by Russian strikes, so they do not lower the Ukrainian score. A 24 July missile hit a Kyiv Oblast arms exhibition killing at least 10, and Ukraine opened criminal proceedings into whether its own officials should have held the event there.

results.name: Iran
results.key_finding: Why it matters: Iran is already near the bottom of the scale and its own conduct confirms that. About 1,500 prisoners under sentence of death began a hunger strike at Ghezel Hesar Prison on 13 July 2026, some sewing their lips shut, with several in critical condition and no official response.

results.name: Democratic Republic of C
results.key_finding: Why it matters: the killings that flagged the DR Congo were carried out by a non-state armed group. At least 16 people died in a suspected ADF attack at Mandeite and Ndiapanda on 22 July 2026, while the recent conduct of the state itself was beating protesters opposing a term-extension law.

results.name: Palestine
results.key_finding: Why it matters: the West Bank killings were inflicted on Palestinians by Israeli settlers and soldiers, so they do not lower the Palestinian score. Four Palestinians were killed at al-Tal near Nablus on 24 July 2026 and nearly 50 more were arrested in raids on about 70 homes.

results.name: Israel
results.key_finding: Why it matters: Israel is already at the absolute floor of 0 out of 100. Human Rights Watch said on 24 July 2026 that the government did not prevent the settler attacks on Tal village and warned the surge in settler violence threatens mass atrocities, which confirms the floor but cannot push the score lower.

results.name: Ally Financial
results.key_finding: Why it matters: no news is a finding in itself. Ally Financial was assessed on rotation with no compassion-relevant evidence in the window, so the score rests on standing structure including the fair-lending regime built after its 2013 auto-lending discrimination settlement.

results.name: Huntington Bancshares
results.key_finding: Why it matters: no news is a finding in itself. Huntington was assessed on rotation with no in-window evidence. The Federal Reserve October 2025 merger order found an excellent level of community development investments, offset by 63 Dallas job cuts from the Veritex integration.

results.name: Freddie Mac
results.key_finding: Why it matters: no news is a finding in itself. Freddie Mac was assessed on rotation with no in-window evidence, and its national loss-mitigation programmes hold the score steady even as nearly 119,000 US properties entered foreclosure in the first quarter of 2026.

results.name: Halcon Resources
results.key_finding: Why it matters: this index entry may no longer describe a real company. Halcon Resources filed for Chapter 11 in August 2019 and was renamed Battalion Oil Corporation in January 2020, which is flagged as a data-integrity issue for index maintenance rather than a scoring change.

results.name: Enservco
results.key_finding: Why it matters: an index entity that has stopped reporting cannot be verified. Enservco has not filed an annual or quarterly report with the SEC since December 2024 and has contracted to a single business line, which is flagged for index review.

notes: BACKFILL RUN. This is the assessor stage for the 2026-07-25 night, reconstructed on 2026-07-27. assessment_date is 2026-07-25 in every artifact. No digest, no briefings, no index writes, no proposal applications. DATE DISCIPLINE. No evidence dated after 2026-07-25 was scored, cited or referenced. Every score-moving source was fetched or searched and its publication date verified against the source itself. Background sources older than the 2026-07-11 to 2026-07-25 window are used only for standing structural context and are labelled with their true dates. CLAIMS DROPPED ON DATE VERIFICATION. Two. (1) MICROSOFT AI: the scan reported that Microsoft was sued over 2026 mass layoffs of roughly 9,000 employees, about 4 per cent of the workforce. That figure is the July 2025 Microsoft layoff, verified against TechCrunch of 2 July 2025 and corroborated by Bloomberg, CNBC and CNN of the same date. The genuine 2026 figure is about 4,800 roles, or 2.1 per cent of the workforce, announced 6 July 2026 per Insurance Journal of 7 July 2026, which also records a separate voluntary buyout offer to roughly 7 per cent of US staff. The scan conflated the two. The 2025 figure was not scored. (2) UKRAINE: the scan attributed at least 14 dead in Kyiv on 24 July 2026 to UN News story 1167875. Direct fetch shows that article is dated 6 July 2026 and describes the 6 July Kyiv attack in which at least 14 civilians were killed and more than 80 injured. The claim was re-dated to its true date and treated as pre-window background. The verified 24 July 2026 event is a Russian ballistic missile strike on an arms exhibition in Kyiv Oblast that killed at least 10 and injured more than 100, corroborated by Kyiv Independent and Ukrainska Pravda of 24 July 2026. The scan claim of more than 150 civilian casualties front-line-wide in 24 hours could not be corroborated by any dated primary source and was not scored. MIXED-SOURCING CAVEATS FROM THE GATE, ALL FOUR RESOLVED. (1) ISOMORPHIC LABS: the DeepMind bioresilience blog post was flagged undated. Direct fetch confirms publication 16 July 2026, and the Axios piece of the same date corroborates. Caveat cleared. (2) UPS: both sources fetched and dates verified directly, The Spokesman-Review 13 July 2026 and Sahm Capital 15 July 2026. Caveat cleared. (3) CLEARVIEW AI: the Justia opinion page returned HTTP 403. Biometric Update was fetched, dated 14 July 2026, and quotes the Seventh Circuit opinion of 13 July 2026 directly. Caveat cleared with the fetch failure noted in the report. (4) ISRAEL: the HRW piece was fetched and its date verified as 24 July 2026, corroborated by Al Jazeera of 24 and 25 July 2026 and CBC of 24 July 2026. Caveat cleared. CHANGE PROPOSALS. One, and it is routed as flag-for-review rather than as a recommended downgrade. MICROSOFT AI, published 81.4, assessed 75.9, delta -5.5. The evidence is real and negative: about 4,800 roles cut announced 6 July 2026, WARN Act compliance investigations by two law firms into the Redmond mass layoff notice of 6 July 2026, 213 Elder Scrolls Online staff cut per a Maryland WARN disclosure reported 9 July 2026, and union legal action over the Xbox layoffs reported 17 July 2026. Only two subdimensions moved on that evidence, B1 Self-Sustainability and I3 Internal Consistency, both 4 to 3. However the resulting composite crosses from Exemplary into Established, and the band-crossing sourcing bar requires at least two distinct sources with at least one at sourceTier 4 or above. No source at tier 4 or above exists for this claim set; the best are tier 2 business press and law-firm notices and one tier 1 advocacy site. The proposal is therefore filed with recommendation flag-for-review and status pending, for human judgment on whether the sourcing supports a band move. An attribution caveat is recorded: the layoffs are Microsoft Corporation conduct while the index entity is the Microsoft AI division. ANTI-FALSE-POSITIVE SCREENING. All 20 entities were screened. APPLIED_CHANGES.md and the July 2026 digests contain no score-change entry for any of the 20, so no stale-baseline rationale was asserted against a documented recent assessment. Directionality was checked on every entity: no entity that surfaced on negative within-window evidence produced an upgrade. Three near-flat positives were checked and reduced to zero or near-zero because the drift was assessor variance rather than evidence: Freddie Mac initially reconstructed at +2.5 with no in-window evidence at all and was re-scored to exactly 62.5; Palestine initially reconstructed at +0.6 on evidence that is entirely harm inflicted by Israel and was re-scored to exactly 25.0; DR Congo initially reconstructed at +0.8 on ADF attacks by a non-state actor and was re-scored to 2.5, a delta of +0.2. It was re-scored to 8.1 and confirmed with a watch flag. ATTRIBUTION RULE APPLIED. Six entities. MATH HYGIENE. Canonical reconstruction (computeCompositeFromDimensions, methodology v1.2, including the integration premium term) reproduced every published composite exactly for all 20 entities. Maximum absolute difference 0.00. No math-hygiene issues found. SUBDIMENSION QUANTISATION NOTE. Subdimension anchors are integers 1 to 5, so a dimension mean can only take multiples of 0.2. Published dimension values ending in .5 (and the DR Congo values of 1.125 and 1.1) are not reproducible from five integer anchors. Where a dimension had no in-window evidence either way, its published .5 value was resolved to the nearest achievable value in the direction the evidence supports, usually the conservative lower value. This accounts for most of the small negative deltas on Ally Financial, Huntington Bancshares, Jordan, Nicaragua, Papua New Guinea and Isomorphic Labs. It is a measurement artifact, not a conduct finding. BAND OBSERVATIONS WITHOUT BAND CHANGES. Two confirmations landed in a different band from their published value while remaining inside the 5-point threshold: Honduras assessed 18.8 Critical against published 20.3 Developing, and Papua New Guinea assessed 20.0 Critical against published 20.3 Developing.
